title: Multiplication Table Grid
story: Remember those multiplication tables from elementary school? The 12x12 grid where row meets column at the product? Building one programmatically is a perfect exercise in nested loops — the code pattern that powers everything from chess boards to image processing.
why: Nested loops are essential for grid-based problems. Building a multiplication table teaches row/column iteration, formatting, and loop nesting.
analogy: A spreadsheet grid where rows and columns intersect to form cells. Each cell = row_header × column_header. Your nested loop is Excel's calculation engine — for every row, compute every column. Simple, systematic, powerful.
try_it: Add a header row showing column numbers 1-N. Add row labels at the start of each row. Make the grid size configurable — try 5x5 and 15x15. Highlight perfect squares (1, 4, 9, 16...) with a different marker.
tips: Outer loop = rows, inner loop = columns — the standard grid pattern
Use consistent width for formatting or columns won't align
Start rows and columns at 1 since multiplication tables are 1-indexed
common_mistakes: Swapping row and column loops — outer must be rows, inner columns
Forgetting to print a newline after each row completes
Starting at 0 instead of 1 — multiplication by 0 is always 0
